title: Inspector: expanding Node progress on a long single-line value widens the whole page
body:
Found by the independent QA of WP-F3 (#243, PR #376, QA round 2, `docs/qa/2026-10-22-wp-f3-qa/round-2/README.md`, finding QA-243-R2-02). Not a #243 behaviour; `apps/web/src/runs/inspector/ProgressDrawer.tsx` is unchanged by that PR; pre-existing on `main`. Recorded in the I01-I07 delivery register (section 7).

## Defect

Expanding **Node progress** on a run whose progress or usage value renders as one long unbroken line widens the whole document instead of wrapping or scrolling inside the drawer.

| Viewport | Before Node progress | After Node progress |
| -------- | -------------------- | ------------------- |
| 1440 px  | 1440 px              | 2123 px             |
| 390 px   | 390 px               | 1508 px             |

## Reproduction

1. Run a loop whose inference turn produces a long single-line result (the fake Claude CLI with a 20,000-character output suffices).
2. Open the run in the inspector and expand Node progress.
3. Measure `document.documentElement.scrollWidth` before and after.

Expected: the content fits the viewport; any large value wraps or scrolls within its own panel.
Actual: horizontal page overflow at both widths.

## Likely cause

The drawer's rows are grid items; a grid item's minimum content width follows its longest unbreakable word, and `break-words` (`overflow-wrap: break-word`) does not constrain min-content sizing. `min-w-0` on the grid children with `overflow-wrap: anywhere` (or `break-all` on the code spans) on the row should fix it.

## Acceptance

- No horizontal document overflow after expanding Node progress at 390 px and 1440 px with a long single-line value.
- Existing Node progress tests and the inspector Edge spec pass.
